play_summaries.Smash Concept: HOW IT WORKS: The outside receiver runs a short hitch while the inside receiver runs a corner route behind it, creating a high-low read that forces the defense to choose. GOOD AGAINST: Cover 2, Zone Coverage — the hitch occupies the underneath defender while the corner route attacks the space behind them. BAD AGAINST: Man Coverage, Cover 3 — man defenders can follow their receivers, while Cover 3 provides a deep defender to protect against the corner route.
play_summaries.Mesh Concept: HOW IT WORKS: Two receivers cross underneath the defense on shallow routes, creating traffic and forcing defenders to navigate the crossing routes. GOOD AGAINST: Rush Blitz, Man Coverage — the routes develop quickly against a blitz, while man defenders can get caught in the crossing routes and lose separation. BAD AGAINST: Zone Coverage, Cover 2 — zone defenders can pass receivers between zones instead of chasing them, while Cover 2's underneath defenders can sit on the crossing routes.
play_summaries.Levels Concept: HOW IT WORKS: Receivers attack the same area of the field at different depths, giving the quarterback multiple options and forcing defenders to cover several levels. GOOD AGAINST: Zone Coverage, Cover 3 — the different route depths create gaps between defenders and can attack the spaces underneath and between deep zones. BAD AGAINST: Rush Blitz, Man Coverage — the deeper routes need time to develop, while man defenders can simply follow their assigned receivers.
play_summaries.Four Verticals: HOW IT WORKS: Multiple receivers run deep vertical routes, stretching the defense across the entire field and attacking the seams between deep defenders. GOOD AGAINST: Cover 2, Goal Line Stand — four vertical routes can overload Cover 2's two deep defenders, while a defense focused heavily near the goal line can leave opportunities behind it. BAD AGAINST: Cover 3, Prevent — three deep defenders divide the field more effectively against vertical routes, while Prevent adds even more deep coverage.
play_summaries.Post-Corner: HOW IT WORKS: A receiver initially attacks the middle of the field with a post before breaking back toward the corner, forcing the defender to change direction twice. GOOD AGAINST: Man Coverage, Cover 2 — the sharp route changes can create separation against man defenders, while the corner break can attack the space between the Cover 2 corner and safety. BAD AGAINST: Cover 3, Prevent — Cover 3 provides deep outside protection while also having help toward the middle, and Prevent adds extra deep defenders.
play_summaries.Slant-Vertical: HOW IT WORKS: One receiver attacks underneath with a quick slant while another stretches the defense vertically, forcing defenders to defend both short and deep threats. GOOD AGAINST: Rush Blitz, Man Coverage — the slant gives the quarterback a quick option against pressure, while the vertical route can pull defenders away from the slant. BAD AGAINST: Zone Coverage, Cover 3 — zone defenders can stay positioned over the slant while another defender handles the vertical route, and Cover 3 provides layered coverage against both.
play_summaries.Flood Concept: HOW IT WORKS: Multiple receivers attack the same side of the field at different depths, overwhelming the defenders responsible for that area. GOOD AGAINST: Cover 2, Zone Coverage — the layered routes force defenders to divide their attention and can overload a single zone. BAD AGAINST: Man Coverage, Prevent — man defenders can each stay with their assigned receiver, while Prevent places extra defenders deep and reduces the effectiveness of the deeper routes.
play_summaries.Out & Up: HOW IT WORKS: A receiver first runs an out route to make the defender expect a short outside break, then turns upfield into a deep route. GOOD AGAINST: Man Coverage, Rush Blitz — the initial out can cause a man defender to commit outside before the receiver goes deep, while the quarterback can also use the quick out against a blitz. BAD AGAINST: Zone Coverage, Prevent — zone defenders do not have to follow the initial out and can remain positioned against the deep route, while Prevent provides extra deep coverage.
play_summaries.Jet Sweep: HOW IT WORKS: A receiver moves horizontally across the formation before taking the handoff, attacking the edge and forcing the defense to move laterally. GOOD AGAINST: Zone Coverage, Prevent — the horizontal motion can pull zone defenders out of position and attack space on the edge, while Prevent focuses heavily on stopping deep passes. BAD AGAINST: Rush Blitz, Goal Line Stand — aggressive defenders can penetrate before the sweep reaches the edge, while a goal-line defense has defenders packed close to the line with little room to turn the corner.

defense_summaries.Rush Blitz: HOW IT WORKS: Sends extra defenders toward the quarterback to create pressure quickly, sacrificing some coverage to get into the backfield faster. GOOD AGAINST: Jet Sweep, Long Pass Routes — the extra pressure can reach the backfield before a Jet Sweep reaches the edge and can disrupt long routes before they develop. BAD AGAINST: Quick Passes (Mesh, Slants) — quick routes get the ball out before the blitz can reach the quarterback, allowing receivers to gain yards in the space left by the blitzing defenders.
defense_summaries.Man Coverage: HOW IT WORKS: Each defender is assigned a specific receiver and follows them wherever they run, preventing receivers from easily finding open zones. GOOD AGAINST: Deep Pass Concepts (Four Verticals) — defenders stay directly with their assigned receivers instead of having to divide large areas of the field between multiple deep routes. BAD AGAINST: Rub Routes (Mesh, Post-Corner) — crossing and sharply changing routes can create traffic and separation, making it difficult for defenders to stay with their assignments.
defense_summaries.Zone Coverage: HOW IT WORKS: Defenders are responsible for specific areas of the field rather than individual receivers, allowing them to watch the quarterback and react to routes entering their zones. GOOD AGAINST: Quick Passes, Out Routes — defenders can remain positioned in the areas targeted by short routes and quickly close on receivers after the catch. BAD AGAINST: Flood & Smash Concepts — multiple receivers attacking the same area at different depths can force one defender to choose which route to cover, creating openings in the zone.
defense_summaries.Cover 2: HOW IT WORKS: Two deep safeties divide the field while underneath defenders protect the short and intermediate areas, creating strong coverage underneath. GOOD AGAINST: Short Runs, Underneath Passes — defenders are positioned close enough to the line and underneath routes to quickly stop short gains. BAD AGAINST: Deep Corners & Smash Concepts — deep corner routes can attack the space between the cornerback and safety, while Smash forces those defenders to choose between a short and deep route.
defense_summaries.Cover 3: HOW IT WORKS: Three deep defenders divide the field into thirds while underneath defenders cover shorter areas, providing strong protection against deep passes. GOOD AGAINST: Deep Bombs (Four Verticals, Post-Corner) — three deep defenders provide more help against multiple vertical routes and reduce the open space available downfield. BAD AGAINST: Levels & Quick Slants — receivers attacking different depths can create gaps between the underneath and deep defenders, while quick slants can reach open areas before the zone closes.
defense_summaries.Prevent: HOW IT WORKS: Drops extra defenders deep downfield to prevent large passing plays, sacrificing underneath coverage and short-yardage defense. GOOD AGAINST: Deep Endzone Passes — the extra deep defenders make it difficult for receivers to get behind the defense near the end zone. BAD AGAINST: Underneath Runs & Quick Chunk Plays — with defenders positioned farther downfield, short runs and quick passes can gain steady yards underneath before defenders can close in.
defense_summaries.Goal Line Stand: HOW IT WORKS: Packs defenders close to the line of scrimmage and concentrates coverage around the end zone, prioritizing stopping short-yardage plays. GOOD AGAINST: Inside Runs & Short Goal Line Passes — the defense has extra bodies near the line, making it difficult for runners to push through and receivers to find immediate openings. BAD AGAINST: Four Verticals — committing heavily to the line leaves fewer defenders available deep, allowing vertical routes to attack space behind the defense.
